note: Frozen cross-language vectors for outOfHoursLine (spec 2026-08-03, review fix I2 2026-08-04, wording revised in a later I2 fix same day). The whole point of this string is that the guardian's PWA and the ward's own device say IDENTICAL words about the same fact — there is no guardian-only variant of the FORMATTER (the two sides do feed it different, per-device numbers — see each formatter's own doc). Two independent implementations exist because TypeScript and Kotlin can't share code: apps/charter-app/src/insights/usageHistory.ts (outOfHoursLine, TS) and android/app/src/main/kotlin/org/forgesworn/charter/ui/GroupMirror.kt (outOfHoursLine, Kotlin). Both consume THIS file so a one-sided edit to either formatter shows up as a failing test, not a silently divergent sentence. Consumers: apps/charter-app/src/insights/usageHistory.test.ts, android/app/src/test/kotlin/org/forgesworn/charter/ui/GroupMirrorTest.kt. `expected: null` means the function returns null/None (nothing to say). 'so far this week' (not plain 'this week'): this line resets on a CALENDAR week while the adjacent weekly-total line is a ROLLING 7 days — without its own scope word the two would print the same phrase for two different windows, and a Monday reset would read as 'the night use stopped' rather than 'the counter rolled over'.
